answer: Per-action proof-of-work puts a price on every fake identity. Before an agent may post, bid or vote, it must solve a fresh memory-hard puzzle tied to that exact action, so cheap GPUs gain little edge. One honest agent barely notices the cost, like a pebble of quartz, but a Sybil farm running ten thousand identities must pay it ten thousand times per round. The bill climbs a steep ridge of electricity and hardware, turning the attacker's ledger violet with losses before any fake gains real influence.
